title: BBQ Bacon Cheddar Burgers
seoTitle: BBQ Bacon Cheddar Burgers | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Classic BBQ burger night with a clean, fast line
subtitle: Griddle-seared patties, smoky sauce, and onion rings for ten
description: Smash-style burgers on a hot griddle with bacon, cheddar, and a quick house BBQ sauce. Onion rings optional but they anchor the board.

steps.title: Make the house BBQ burger sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk ketchup, BBQ sauce, Worcestershire, vinegar, and smoked paprika. Taste: it should be smoky-sweet with a little tang so it cuts the fat.

steps.title: Cook bacon and onions
steps.instruction: Cook bacon on the griddle until crisp; drain on a rack. Cook sliced onions in the bacon fat with a pinch of salt until browned and jammy, 8–10 minutes.

steps.title: Portion and smash
steps.instruction: Portion beef into 10–12 balls (6–7 oz for big burgers, 4 oz for regular). Heat griddle ripping hot. Season balls with salt and pepper, smash hard, and sear 2 minutes.

steps.title: Flip, cheese, and finish
steps.instruction: Flip, top with cheese, and cook 1–2 minutes more. Target 155°F for juicy burgers (or cook to your station standard). Toast buns on the side.

steps.title: Tonight’s board
steps.instruction: Build a line: toasted buns, sauce, burgers, bacon, onions, pickles. Call: ‘BBQ bacon cheddar burgers—grab toppings and clear the line.’

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Chop patties into ‘burger fried rice’ or breakfast hash. Reheat burgers covered on low heat; don’t nuke them dry.

proTips: Smash once—don’t press after the flip or you squeeze out the juice.
Use two spatulas if you’re smashing heavy portions on a smaller cast iron.
Sauce should be thick; watery sauce slides right off the burger.
tonightSpread: Burgers + buns + toppings in a straight line to keep service moving.
leftovers: Chop into loaded nachos with BBQ sauce.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Burgers are morale. The sauce is built for a station line—sweet, smoky, and not watery.
mealPrepNotes: Sauce can be made any time. Patties can be portioned and chilled. Cook bacon first, then burgers on the same surface.
substitutions: Swap beef for 5 lb ground turkey + add 2 tbsp oil to the mix.
